segments.label: §68, de source block1
segments.text: Das Wort entsteht erst durch den Accent, der ihm die Einheit des Begriffes einhaucht.

segments.label: §68, de source block2
segments.text: Wenn sich in einem einfachen Worte zwei ganz gleiche Betonungen fänden, so stellte sich die Einheit des Begriffs nicht sinnlich auch vor dem Ohre dar, und die Angemessenheit der Begleitung des Gedanken durch den Laut wäre gestört.

segments.label: §68, de source block3
segments.text: Das natürliche Sprachgefühl würde dadurch zu sehr verletzt, als dass man sich den Fall möglich denken könnte.

segments.label: §68, de source block4
segments.text: Zwei in einem Worte aus zwei verschiedenen zusammenkommende Accente werden sich daher in der Aussprache einer dem andren unterordnen, oder die Begriffe der einzelnen Wörter müssten sich denn nicht in Einen verbinden; denn alsdann waltet nothwendig ein Element vor.

segments.label: §68, de source block5
segments.text: Da der Accent durch die feste Stelle, die er im Worte einnimmt, dessen Individualität vollenden hilft, so können durch Verschiedenheit der Betonung aus der gleichen Sylbenfolge verschiedene Wörter entstehen, und es darf nicht in Verwunderung setzen, dass dies auch in Sprachen ganz ungebildeter Nationen angetroffen wird.

segments.label: §68, de source block6
segments.text: Es ist eine sehr gewöhnliche Bemerkung, dass den Fremden bei den gemeinsten Volksklassen nichts so unverständlich macht, als unrichtige Betonung.

segments.label: §68, de source block7
segments.text: Gerade der Ungebildete in Nationen und Ständen ist gewohnt, jedes Wort unzergliedert als ein Ganzes zu nehmen, dessen Physiognomie, wenn man so sagen darf, er an dem Accente erkennt.

segments.label: §68, codex source block1
segments.text: The word comes into being only through accent, which breathes into it the unity of the concept.

segments.label: §68, codex source block2
segments.text: If a simple word contained two entirely equal accentuations, the unity of the concept would not also be presented to the ear through the senses, and the appropriateness of sound’s accompaniment of thought would be disturbed.

segments.label: §68, codex source block3
segments.text: This would violate the natural feeling for language too greatly for one to conceive the case as possible.

segments.label: §68, codex source block4
segments.text: Two accents coming together in one word from two different words will therefore be subordinated one to the other in pronunciation, unless the concepts of the individual words fail to combine into one; for when they do combine, one element necessarily predominates.

segments.label: §68, codex source block5
segments.text: Since accent, through the fixed place it occupies in the word, helps to complete the word’s individuality, different words can arise from the same sequence of syllables through differences of accentuation, and it should occasion no surprise that this is also found in the languages of entirely uncultivated nations.

segments.label: §68, codex source block6
segments.text: It is a very common observation that nothing makes a foreigner so unintelligible to the lowest classes of the people as incorrect accentuation.

segments.label: §68, codex source block7
segments.text: It is precisely the uncultivated person, among nations and social ranks alike, who is accustomed to taking each word, unanalysed, as a whole whose physiognomy, if one may put it so, is recognised by its accent.

segments.label: §68, muse source block1
segments.text: The word arises only through accent, which breathes the unity of the concept into it.

segments.label: §68, muse source block2
segments.text: If two quite equal accentuations were found in a simple word, the unity of the concept would not also present itself sensibly before the ear, and the appropriateness of the accompaniment of thought by sound would be disturbed.

segments.label: §68, muse source block3
segments.text: The natural feeling for language would be too much violated by this for one to be able to think the case possible.

segments.label: §68, muse source block4
segments.text: Two accents coming together in one word from two different words will therefore in pronunciation subordinate themselves, one to the other, unless the concepts of the individual words are not to combine into one; for then one element necessarily prevails.

segments.label: §68, muse source block5
segments.text: Since accent, through the fixed place it occupies in the word, helps to complete the word's individuality, different words can arise from the same sequence of syllables through difference of accentuation, and it must not cause surprise that this is also met with in languages of quite uncultivated nations.

segments.label: §68, muse source block6
segments.text: It is a very common observation that nothing makes the foreigner so unintelligible among the commonest classes of the people as incorrect accentuation.

segments.label: §68, muse source block7
segments.text: Precisely the uneducated person, in nations and in social estates, is accustomed to take each word unanalysed as a whole whose physiognomy, if one may so say, he recognizes by the accent.

segments.label: §68, astra source block1
segments.text: The word comes into being only through accent, which breathes the unity of the concept into it.

segments.label: §68, astra source block2
segments.text: If two entirely equal accents occurred in a simple word, the unity of the concept would not be made perceptible to the ear as well, and the aptness of sound as an accompaniment to thought would be impaired.

segments.label: §68, astra source block3
segments.text: This would so offend the natural feeling for language that one could not conceive of such a case as possible.

segments.label: §68, astra source block4
segments.text: Thus, when two accents come together in a single word from two different words, one will be subordinated to the other in pronunciation, unless the concepts of the individual words fail to combine into one; for when they do combine, one element necessarily predominates.

segments.text: It is a very common observation that nothing makes a foreigner so unintelligible to the lowest social classes as incorrect accentuation.

segments.text: It is precisely the uncultivated person, in nations and social ranks alike, who is accustomed to taking each word unanalyzed as a whole and recognizing its physiognomy, if one may put it so, by its accent.

segments.label: §69, de source block1
segments.text: Obgleich mehrere Worte eigentlich bloss durch den Redeaccent verbunden werden, so geschieht dies in einigen Fällen doch auch durch den wahren Sprachaccent, nur dass alsdann die verbundenen Theile nicht, wie in jenem Fall, ihre ihnen eigenthümlichen Accente unverändert erhalten.

segments.label: §69, de source block2
segments.text: Man sieht leicht, dass ich hier an die enklitischen Wörter erinnern will, die es aber bei weitem nicht bloss im Griechischen, sondern wenn man genau darauf achtet, in allen Sprachen giebt und geben muss.

segments.label: §69, de source block3
segments.text: Denn in allen ist der Fall vorhanden, dass für sich bestehende Wörter in eine solche Lage gegen andre treten, dass ihre selbständige Geltung ganz in der Anschliessung an diese aufgeht.

segments.label: §69, de source block4
segments.text: Damit aber fällt von selbst auch ihre eigenthümliche Betonung dahin.

segments.label: §69, de source block5
segments.text: In der so scharf accentuirten Englischen Sprache hört man dies, und zwar gerade auch im Volk, ungemein stark, und so dass die ganze Lautgeltung der enklitischen Wörter dadurch verändert wird.

segments.label: §69, de source block6
segments.text: Wie dadurch auch der Accent des an sich reissenden Worts eine andre Stelle oder einen zweiten, jedoch wohl nicht gleich starken Accent neben sich erhalten kann, beruht auf Regeln und Gewohnheiten einzelner Sprachen, so wie auch, ob es für die Gattung von Wörtern, die angehängt werden können, doppelte Lautformen, eine orthotonische und enklitische, geben soll.

segments.label: §69, de source block7
segments.text: Da in der Sanskrita Sprache zu dem Wort- und Redeaccent noch die genaue Bewahrung des Zeitmasses und die Wortverkettung durch Buchstabenveränderung hinzukam, so muss, bei dem ausserdem so grossen Umfange des Alphabets, ihr Lautsystem vorzüglich schwierig, aber auch ungemein reich und mannigfaltig gewesen seyn.

segments.label: §69, codex source block1
segments.text: Although several words are properly joined only through discourse accent, in some cases they are also joined through true linguistic accent, except that the connected parts then do not retain their own accents unchanged, as they do in the former case.

segments.label: §69, codex source block2
segments.text: It is easy to see that I mean here to recall enclitic words, which, however, exist by no means only in Greek, but, if one attends closely, exist and must exist in all languages.

segments.label: §69, codex source block3
segments.text: For in all languages there are cases in which words that stand independently enter into such a relation to others that their independent force is wholly absorbed in their attachment to them.

segments.label: §69, codex source block4
segments.text: With this, their own distinctive accentuation also falls away of itself.

segments.label: §69, codex source block5
segments.text: In the so sharply accentuated English language, this can be heard with extraordinary force, precisely among the common people too, and in such a way that the entire sound value of the enclitic words is thereby altered.

segments.label: §69, codex source block6
segments.text: How this can also cause the accent of the word that draws the other to itself to occupy a different position, or to acquire beside it a second accent, though probably not an equally strong one, depends on the rules and habits of individual languages; so too does whether the kind of words that can be attached is to have two sound forms, an orthotonic and an enclitic one.

segments.label: §69, codex source block7
segments.text: Since Sanskrit added to word accent and discourse accent the exact preservation of temporal measure and the chaining of words through letter change, its sound system, with the already very great range of its alphabet, must have been particularly difficult, but also extraordinarily rich and manifold.

segments.label: §69, muse source block1
segments.text: Although several words are properly connected only by speech-accent, in some cases this does also happen through true language-accent, except that then the connected parts do not, as in the former case, retain unchanged the accents peculiar to them.

segments.label: §69, muse source block2
segments.text: One sees easily that I wish here to recall enclitic words, which however exist very far from only in Greek; rather, if one attends closely to it, they exist and must exist in all languages.

segments.label: §69, muse source block3
segments.text: For in all of them the case occurs that words existing by themselves enter into such a position in relation to others that their independent validity is wholly absorbed in their attaching themselves to these.

segments.label: §69, muse source block4
segments.text: But with that their peculiar accentuation also falls away of itself.

segments.label: §69, muse source block5
segments.text: In English, accentuated so sharply, one hears this extremely strongly, and precisely also among the common people, and in such a way that the whole sound-validity of the enclitic words is thereby changed.

segments.label: §69, muse source block6
segments.text: How the accent of the word that pulls the other to itself can thereby also receive another place, or beside itself a second, though probably not equally strong, accent, rests on rules and habits of individual languages, as does also whether there are to be, for the class of words that can be attached, double sound-forms, an orthotonic and an enclitic one.

segments.label: §69, muse source block7
segments.text: Since in the Sanskrit language, in addition to word-accent and speech-accent, there were also exact preservation of time-measure and word-chaining through letter-change, its sound system, with the otherwise so great extent of the alphabet, must have been especially difficult but also extremely rich and manifold.

segments.text: For in all languages there are cases in which words that stand on their own enter into such a relation to others that their independent standing is wholly absorbed in their attachment to those others.

segments.label: §70, de source block1
segments.text: Durch den Redeaccent kann der Sprechende entweder genau das Gewicht bezeichnen, welches jedes Wort und jeder Satz in der Bedeutung der Rede haben, oder die Erhebungen und Senkungen der Stimme nach einer davon unabhängigen in der Sprache zur Gewohnheit gewordenen Methode vertheilen, welcher die Rücksicht auf den Sinn zwar nicht ganz aufgeopfert, aber doch vollkommen untergeordnet wird.

segments.label: §70, de source block2
segments.text: Dieser Unterschied zeigt sich am deutlichsten im Deutschen und Französischen Lesen und Declamiren, da die Franzosen den Deutschen, welcher ihre Sprache, wie die seinige, im Reden accentuirt, des Singens beschuldigen.

segments.label: §70, de source block3
segments.text: Ausser diesen beiden sehr entgegengesetzten Arten giebt es indess viele minder bestimmt nuancirte, die sich alle durch das mehr, oder minder starke Herausheben der Verstandesgeltung der Wörter und Sylben unterscheiden, da wohl jedes Volk hierin einem eignen Gefühl folgt.

segments.label: §70, de source block4
segments.text: Gerade aber weil es von dem wichtigsten Einfluss ist, auf welche Weise die Gedankenfolge in dem lebendigen Vortrage erscheint; so ist dieser Punkt von der grossesten Erheblichkeit für die intellectuelle Bildung, vorzüglich des am meisten auf die lebendige Mittheilung beschränkten Volks.

segments.label: §70, codex source block1
segments.text: Through discourse accent, the speaker can either mark exactly the weight each word and each sentence has in the meaning of the discourse, or distribute the raisings and lowerings of the voice according to a method independent of that meaning that has become habitual in the language, to which regard for the sense is admittedly not entirely sacrificed, but is nevertheless completely subordinated.

segments.label: §70, codex source block2
segments.text: This difference appears most clearly in German and French reading and declamation, since the French accuse a German who accentuates their language in speaking as he does his own of singing.

segments.label: §70, codex source block3
segments.text: Besides these two strongly opposed kinds, however, there are many with less sharply defined nuances, all differing in how strongly they bring out the force of words and syllables for the understanding, since each people probably follows a feeling of its own in this.

segments.label: §70, codex source block4
segments.text: But precisely because the manner in which the sequence of thoughts appears in living delivery has the most important influence, this point is of the greatest significance for intellectual cultivation, especially that of the common people, who are most confined to living communication.

segments.label: §70, muse source block1
segments.text: Through speech-accent the speaker can either designate exactly the weight which each word and each sentence is to have in the meaning of the speech, or distribute the risings and fallings of the voice according to a method, independent of that, that has become habitual in the language, to which regard for sense is indeed not wholly sacrificed but yet completely subordinated.

segments.label: §70, muse source block2
segments.text: This difference shows itself most clearly in German and French reading and declaiming, since the French accuse a German who accentuates their language in speaking as he does his own of singing.

segments.label: §70, muse source block3
segments.text: Besides these two very opposite kinds, however, there are many less definitely nuanced ones, all of which are distinguished by the more or less strong bringing out of the validity of words and syllables for the understanding, since probably every people follows its own feeling in this.

segments.label: §70, muse source block4
segments.text: But precisely because it is of the most important influence in what way the sequence of thoughts appears in living delivery, this point is of the greatest moment for intellectual cultivation, especially of the people most restricted to living communication.

segments.label: §70, astra source block1
segments.text: Through speech accent, the speaker can either mark precisely the weight that each word and each sentence has in the meaning of the speech, or distribute the rises and falls of the voice according to a method that has become habitual in the language and is independent of this weighting; consideration for the sense is not wholly sacrificed to this method, but is nevertheless completely subordinated to it.

segments.label: §70, astra source block2
segments.text: This difference is most evident in German and French reading aloud and declamation, since the French accuse Germans of singing when they accent French in speech as they would their own language.

segments.label: §70, astra source block3
segments.text: Besides these two sharply opposed modes, however, there are many less distinctly differentiated ones, all distinguished by the greater or lesser prominence they give to the significance of words and syllables for the understanding, since each people presumably follows a feeling of its own in this.

segments.label: §70, astra source block4
segments.text: But precisely because the way the sequence of thoughts appears in living delivery has the most important influence, this point is of the greatest significance for intellectual cultivation, especially that of the common people, who are most restricted to living communication.

segments.label: §71, de source block1
segments.text: Von den grossesten und sichtbarsten Folgen für die Ausbildung des Lautsystems ist die Einführung der Buchstabenschrift.

segments.label: §71, de source block2
segments.text: Obgleich der articulirte Ton durch dieselbe niemals dem Gebiete des immer vergehenden Schalles entzogen wird, und nichts, als ein an diesen Schall erinnerndes Zeichen erhält, so wirken diese Zeichen und ihre Vergleichung doch dergestalt auf den Verstand und die Einbildungskraft, dass die Sprachtöne sich bestimmter an die ihnen angewiesenen Punkte heften, und viel klarer in ihrer Elementareigenschaft vor die Seele treten.

segments.label: §71, de source block3
segments.text: An den Zeichen geht die Aussprache einer Generation auf die der andren über, und Abweichungen lassen sich an der Rechtschreibung erkennen, und die Sprachlaute können mit Allem, was zu ihnen gehört, Gegenstand der Betrachtung und der wissenschaftlichen Behandlung werden.

segments.label: §71, de source block4
segments.text: Die Buchstabenschrift führt daher die beiden grossen Vorzüge mit sich, aus welchen sich hernach viele einzelne Folgen durch die ganze Sprache erstrecken : einmal dass alle Lautverhältnisse der Sprache sich reiner und bestimmter gegen einander stellen und ordnen, und vollständiger und systematischer ausgebildet werden, dann dass, indem der Verstand die Grundtheile der Sprache genauer trennt und bestimmter festhält, die Idee ihrer Gliederung lebendiger in ihm wird, und die Vorstellung ihres von den Grundtheilen an aufsteigenden Baues an Anschaulichkeit und Vollständigkeit gewinnt.

segments.label: §71, de source block5
segments.text: Dagegen kann auch durch die wissenschaftliche Bearbeitung der Lautbezeichnungen zu gekünstelte und systematische Behandlung derselben vorzüglich da entstehen, wo Sprachen aus dem lebendigen Volksverkehr in bloss gelehrten Gebrauch überzugehen anfangen.

segments.label: §71, codex source block1
segments.text: The introduction of alphabetic writing has consequences of the greatest and most visible kind for the development of the sound system.

segments.label: §71, codex source block2
segments.text: Although it never removes articulated tone from the realm of sound that is forever passing away, and gives it nothing but a sign recalling that sound, these signs and their comparison nevertheless act upon the understanding and the imagination in such a way that speech tones attach themselves more definitely to their assigned points and appear before the soul much more clearly in their character as elements.

segments.label: §71, codex source block3
segments.text: Through the signs, the pronunciation of one generation passes to that of another; deviations can be recognised in spelling, and speech sounds, with everything belonging to them, can become objects of reflection and scholarly treatment.

segments.label: §71, codex source block4
segments.text: Alphabetic writing therefore brings with it two great advantages, from which many particular consequences subsequently extend throughout the language: first, all the sound relations of the language are set against one another and ordered more purely and definitely, and are developed more completely and systematically; second, as the understanding separates the fundamental parts of language more exactly and holds them more definitely, the idea of its articulation becomes more vivid within it, and the representation of its structure, rising from the fundamental parts upwards, gains in intuitive clarity and completeness.

segments.label: §71, codex source block5
segments.text: On the other hand, scholarly work on the signs for sounds can also give rise to an excessively artificial and systematic treatment of them, especially where languages begin to pass from living intercourse among the people into exclusively learned use.

segments.label: §71, muse source block1
segments.text: Of the greatest and most visible consequences for the development of the sound system is the introduction of alphabetic writing.

segments.label: §71, muse source block2
segments.text: Although articulated tone is never thereby withdrawn from the domain of ever-passing sound, and receives nothing but a sign recalling this sound, these signs and their comparison nevertheless act on the understanding and the imagination in such a way that the tones of language attach themselves more definitely to the points assigned to them, and step before the soul much more clearly in their elementary character.

segments.label: §71, muse source block3
segments.text: By means of the signs, the pronunciation of one generation passes over to that of another, deviations can be recognized in the spelling, and speech sounds, with all that belongs to them, can become an object of contemplation and of scientific treatment.

segments.label: §71, muse source block4
segments.text: Alphabetic writing therefore brings with it the two great advantages from which afterwards many individual consequences extend through the whole language: first, that all sound relations of language place and arrange themselves more purely and definitely in relation to one another and are developed more completely and systematically; then, that, as the understanding separates the fundamental parts of language more exactly and holds them more definitely fast, the idea of their articulation becomes more living in it, and the representation of their structure, ascending from the fundamental parts, gains in intuitive vividness and completeness.

segments.label: §71, muse source block5
segments.text: On the other hand, through scientific working on the sound designations, an excessively artificial and systematic treatment of them can also arise, especially where languages begin to pass from living intercourse among the people into merely learned use.

segments.label: §71, astra source block1
segments.text: The introduction of alphabetic writing has some of the greatest and most visible consequences for the development of the sound system.

segments.label: §71, astra source block2
segments.text: Although alphabetic writing never removes articulated sound from the realm of ever-vanishing audible sound, and gives it nothing but a sign that calls that audible sound to mind, these signs and their comparison nevertheless act upon the understanding and imagination in such a way that speech sounds attach themselves more definitely to their assigned points and present themselves to the soul much more clearly in their character as elements.

segments.label: §71, astra source block3
segments.text: Through the signs, the pronunciation of one generation passes into that of the next; deviations can be recognized in spelling, and speech sounds, together with everything that belongs to them, can become objects of reflection and scholarly study.

segments.label: §71, astra source block4
segments.text: Alphabetic writing thus brings two great advantages, from which many particular consequences subsequently extend throughout the language. First, all the sound relations of the language are set against one another and ordered more cleanly and distinctly, and are developed more completely and systematically. Second, as the understanding separates the basic parts of language more precisely and retains them more distinctly, the idea of language’s organization into parts gains greater life within it, and the representation of its structure, rising from the basic parts upwards, gains in vividness and completeness.

segments.text: On the other hand, scholarly work on the signs for sounds can also lead to an excessively contrived and systematic treatment of them, especially where languages begin to pass from living interaction among the people into exclusively learned use.

segments.label: note:bopp-64, de source block1
segments.text: Die Regeln für die Mitte der Wörter werden genau genommen nicht ganz richtig so genannt. Vollständig gelten sie nur bei der Umstempelung der Wurzel zum Wort, und bei den Flexionen von diesem. Schon bei den, das so gestempelte Wort weiter umformenden Taddhita-Suffixen, treten die Regeln der Anfangs- und Endbuchstaben verschiedener Worte ein. Bopp's Gramm. S. 58. §. 85.

segments.label: note:bopp-64, codex source block1
segments.text: Humboldt’s note: Strictly speaking, the rules for the interior of words are not quite correctly so called. They apply in full only when the root is stamped into a word, and in the inflections of that word. Already with the Taddhita suffixes, which further reshape the word thus stamped, the rules for the initial and final letters of different words come into operation. Bopp’s Grammar, p. 58, § 85.

segments.label: note:bopp-64, muse source block1
segments.text: [Humboldt:] Strictly taken, the rules for the middle of words are not quite correctly so called. They hold completely only in the re-stamping of the root into a word, and in the inflexions from it. Already with the Taddhita suffixes, which further transform the word so stamped, the rules for the initial and final letters of different words come in. Bopp's Grammar, p. 58, § 85.

segments.label: note:bopp-64, astra source block1
segments.text: Humboldt’s note: Strictly speaking, the rules for the interior of words are not quite correctly so called. They apply in full only when the root is stamped anew as a word, and in that word’s inflections. Already with the Taddhita suffixes, which further reshape the word thus stamped, the rules for the initial and final letters of different words come into play. Bopp’s Grammar, p. 58, § 85.

segments.label: note:chinese, de source block1
segments.text: In den Chinesischen Grammatiken werden die Intonationen zwar Modificationen der Wörter, oder was dort auf Eins hinausläuft, der Sylben genannt, was auch in ihnen viel zweckmässiger ist. Allein eigentlich ruhen sie doch nur auf der Vocalendung, und daher ist es, nach Art andrer Sprachen zu reden, natürlicher zu sagen, dass jede einfache und zusammengesetzte Vocalendung diese und diese Intonation haben kann, und nun die Wörter, nach Verschiedenheit ihrer Bedeutung, die so oder so intonirte Vocalendung annehmen. Auf diese Weise stellt sich die Sache den kurzen und langen Vocalen anderer Sprachen gleich.

segments.label: note:chinese, codex source block1
segments.text: Humboldt’s note: In Chinese grammars, intonations are admittedly called modifications of words, or, what there amounts to the same thing, of syllables, which is also much more appropriate in those grammars. Yet strictly speaking they rest only on the vowel ending, and it is therefore more natural, speaking in the manner of other languages, to say that each simple and compound vowel ending can have such and such an intonation, and that words then adopt a vowel ending intoned in one way or another according to differences in their meaning. Viewed in this way, the matter is placed on the same footing as the short and long vowels of other languages.

segments.label: note:chinese, muse source block1
segments.text: [Humboldt:] In Chinese grammars the intonations are indeed called modifications of the words, or, what there amounts to the same thing, of the syllables, which in them is also much more expedient. But properly they rest only on the vowel ending, and hence, to speak after the manner of other languages, it is more natural to say that every simple and compound vowel ending can have this or that intonation, and that the words then, according to the difference of their meaning, assume the vowel ending intoned in one way or the other. In this way the matter puts itself on a level with the short and long vowels of other languages.

segments.label: note:sanskrit-pronouns, de source block1
segments.text: Die Sanskritischen Pronomina der 1. und 2. Person haben zwar für einige Casus, neben der ausführlichen, weil weniger üblichen Form, eine zweite häufiger gebrauchte, abgekürzte. Aber es scheint nicht, dass dieselbe bloss enklitisch gebraucht worden sey.

segments.label: note:sanskrit-pronouns, codex source block1
segments.text: Humboldt’s note: For some cases, the Sanskrit pronouns of the first and second persons do admittedly have, beside the full form, which is less usual, a second, abbreviated form that is used more frequently. But it does not seem that this was used only enclitically.

segments.label: note:sanskrit-pronouns, muse source block1
segments.text: [Humboldt:] The Sanskrit pronouns of the 1st and 2nd person do indeed have for some cases, beside the fuller form, because it is less usual, a second, more frequently used, shortened one. But it does not seem that the latter was used merely enclitically.

segments.label: note:sanskrit-pronouns, astra source block1
segments.text: Humboldt’s note: The Sanskrit pronouns of the first and second persons do have, for certain cases, a second, more frequently used, abbreviated form alongside the full form, whose fullness is due to its less frequent use. But it does not appear that this second form was used exclusively as an enclitic.

But it does not appear that this second form was used exclusively as an enclitic.

But it does not appear that this second form was used exclusively as an enclitic.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Systemsucht is more distinctly pejorative than 'passion for systematization'. The English softens the suspicion that the grammarians' excessive system-making produced some of the rules.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use excessive zeal for systematization to preserve the pejorative Sucht without turning the conjecture into an established accusation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The antecedent of seine in 'erhält seine Freiheit' is not secure. Rhythm or quantity from the preceding sentence is a plausible referent: aesthetic predominance would preserve its freedom against intellectual emphasis. The English 'it preserves its freedom' more readily suggests aesthetic feeling's own freedom. This is an unresolved interpretive concern, not a demonstrated mistranslation.
decision.resolution: Unresolved and retained provisionally. Both rhythm/quantity and aesthetic feeling are grammatically possible. Keep its freedom, with a local translator note explicitly naming the alternatives and no claim that the antecedent has been settled.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: 'Deviations can be recognized in spelling' can locate the deviations in spelling itself. The German presents spelling as the evidence by which deviations are recognized, within an argument about pronunciation transmitted between generations.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use deviations can be detected by reference to spelling, making Rechtschreibung the diagnostic evidence rather than necessarily the location of the deviations.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: rein/reine Geschiedenheit and rein geschieden are rendered as clear/clearly, shifting purity of separation to clarity and conflating rein with Klarheit, inconsistently with Reine Bestimmtheit rendered pure in p59:s3.
decision.resolution: Retained with qualification. Rein geschieden describes the distinctness of sounds; clear separation is idiomatic in these local contexts and is supported by the conditional term rule. Pure/purely is kept where the text predicates purity, not imposed mechanically on every rein. The German lexical pattern remains recoverable.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Veränderung and Verwandlung are both collapsed into change/changing, erasing a recurrent German lexical contrast the audit was warned not to modernize away.
decision.resolution: Declined as an invariant lexical distinction. The neighbouring Veränderung/Verwandlung compounds overlap in these contact-change contexts; the guide records all four German terms and the word-versus-sound bearers. No source-based contrast requires a blanket English change/transformation distinction.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Ton, Laut and Schall are flattened toward sound; p71:s2 loses the Ton/Schall contrast, and Tongebiete is narrowed to accentual domains.
decision.resolution: Retained with explanation. Ton is sound where musical pitch is not at issue; Schall is separately audible, transient sound in71. Tongebiete is accentual domains in the immediately preceding explanation of prominence grouping. The guide exposes the historical overlap instead of creating a false modern tone distinction.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Recurrent Geltung is rendered variously as force, sway, standing and significance, and ideale Geltung becomes conceptual force, losing the cross-block thread of validity/efficacy and the ideal/ideational term.
decision.resolution: Declined as a fixed-equivalent rule. Geltung has different bearers here: conceptual efficacy, quantity’s sway, a word’s independent standing and significance for the understanding. The conditional termbase distinguishes them; a recurring-term entry makes that relationship explicit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The zu...als dass nicht...sollte construction is split and sollte becomes must, strengthening and flattening the negated modal necessity.
decision.resolution: Accepted in part. Remove must from the second English sentence while preserving the first too-closely...not construction and the causal continuation. Splitting the long construction remains an English readability choice; no temporal or conditional clause is dropped.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: durch sie is resolved as Inflection, whereas the pronoun may refer more immediately to individual letter-change in p61:s3; English antecedent choice is not certain.
decision.resolution: Accepted as an unresolved antecedent. Replace Inflection thus brings with This brings, leaving the preceding letter-change/inflection relation open. The double advantage is preserved; the apparatus retains the alternatives.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Bracketed Systematic Account of the Sanskrit Language is an added gloss for the title and renders Lehrgebäude loosely as account.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Retain the citable German book title and remove the added bracketed English title gloss from Humboldt’s note.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Glossing der as the misrepresents its genitive function in the context of p62:s1.
decision.resolution: Accepted in part. Remove the isolated English gloss of der and retain the exact German anchor in the note. The deleted modifier is translated in full and its German wording remains in original source-note metadata; it is not restored into the main text.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: tried to disregard adds attempt where wollte is volitional/hypothetical neglect.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use a foreigner who were to disregard it for the hypothetical wollte, removing the added suggestion of an attempted but unsuccessful disregard.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: individuellen is transferred from habits to tribes, changing scope from individual/particular habits of tribes to habits of individual tribes.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use particular habits of the tribes, keeping the modifier on habits rather than transferring it to tribes.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Present does for elliptical Sanskrit comparison shifts the past-tense claim about Greek word-joining.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use joined words, as in Sanskrit, avoiding an extra English tense choice for the elliptical comparison.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: erscheint...nicht is rendered as is not made...by this means, introducing causative making for appearance.
decision.resolution: Retained. The through-this-means construction itself supplies the causal relation; not made clear to the senses is an idiomatic equivalent of erscheint...nicht...durch dies Mittel. No extra causal agent or claim is introduced. The sensory and boundary qualifications remain.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Zeitmass as bare Quantity adopts later classical-prosody terminology and obscures the time-measure sense active in p65:s6; defensible but not transparent for historical vocabulary.
decision.resolution: Retained with guide. Quantity is an established readable rendering of temporal quantity and is defined locally as timing and duration, not assumed to mean mere amount or vowel length alone. It remains distinct from accent. No modern theory is silently assigned to the historical term.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Dropping nicht in ob...nicht auch neutralizes the negative-question bias toward suspecting short e and o existed.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restore whether the living language did not also possess a short e and o, preserving the negative-question orientation as well as uncertainty.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: language taken in isolation adds taken and weakens unverbundenen, i.e. language apart from connected discourse.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use language outside connected discourse to clarify unverbundenen without turning the parts themselves into a new type of isolated language.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: alsdann is resolved as when they do combine, but its nearest textual antecedent is the negative alternative; the English logic is plausible yet interpretively certain where German is compressed.
decision.resolution: Qualified, interpretation retained. In the surrounding argument, one element’s predominance explains conceptual union, not failure of union. Keep when they do combine, while a local translator note explicitly records that alsdann is compressed and the alternative attachment is possible.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: whose fullness is due to its less frequent use makes an explicit causal claim from the compressed weil phrase; the parallelism supports it, but German does not state the causal verb in that form.
decision.resolution: Declined omission of weil. The causal connective is explicit in the German; the source-based reading preserves fuller because less usual. The final wording can be less cumbersome, but may not silently reduce the cause to a coordinate property or reverse it.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Eingehen in das Ganze becomes investigation, importing the noun from Sprachuntersuchung in p56:s1 and losing entering into/engaging with.
decision.resolution: Accepted in part. Replace investigation of the language system with engagement with the language system; this preserves Eingehen without repeating Sprachuntersuchung from the previous block.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Gliederung is rendered organization into parts here, against articulation for Gliederung in p64:s3 and p64:s8, weakening a key cross-block membering/articulation thread.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use articulation into parts in71, retaining the Gliederung thread and its local operation without mechanically substituting the same phrase for all contexts.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: gemeinsten Volksklassen as lowest social classes turns commonest into lowest in rank.
decision.resolution: Qualified. Gemeinsten can denote the socially lowest or most ordinary/common classes in this historical context. Use commonest classes of the people to avoid an unnecessarily sharp rank claim while retaining the social-class reference. No neutral modern sociological label is attributed to Humboldt.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: does not in every language wholly shed is scope-ambiguous in English between not in all and in none, where German nicht in allen Sprachen indicates not in all.
decision.resolution: Retained. Does not in every language means not in all, as in the German; it does not assert in none. The contrast and subsequent finding in both African and highly developed languages make the scope explicit. No awkward inversion is necessary.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: What are letters in this division
decision.resolution: Retain letters and alphabet, with the spoken bearer explained in the note and guide. They are not silently replaced with phonemes; writing is introduced separately.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Intellectualitaet and the bearer of the quality
decision.resolution: Use intellectual character of language here, in accordance with the local conditional term rule. Earlier intellectual life of a nation remains unchanged; neither is a psychometric score.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Ton against accompanying noise
decision.resolution: Use sound rather than forcing tone where musical pitch is not the point. Preserve the normative purification claim as Humboldt’s; the guide distinguishes overlapping German words.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Sound impressions and historical evaluation
decision.resolution: Retain clicking, blaring, hissing, rasping and breathing as approximate auditory descriptions, not certified modern classes. Preserve the author’s developmental evaluation; the focused IPA note qualifies the assimilation of clicks to animal residue.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Continuum and fixing
decision.resolution: The continuous range belongs to articulatory movement; a particular sound occupies a habitual point in it. Do not turn this into an assertion that a language has no discrete sound distinctions.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Matter and reciprocal action
decision.resolution: Use material for resistant Stoff and preserve influence in both directions, the mind’s asserted ascendancy and its repeated limitation. The causal theory remains attributed.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Sound differentiation and conceptual clarity
decision.resolution: Retain the strong dependence asserted in the German. The note identifies this as a theoretical inference without a comparative demonstration in this division.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Inflection and chronology
decision.resolution: Letter changes mark distinctions; all inflection is said to originate here, whether simultaneous with language or later. Preserve the chronological alternatives and avoid treating every sound change as inflection.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Meaningless sound and a subsidiary concept
decision.resolution: Keep meaningless in itself and subsidiary concept; this contrasts unnecessary lexical content with formal indication, not grammatical function with its absence.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Material in thought and the sign of form
decision.resolution: Use material rather than physical sound alone; the bearer has shifted to represented content. Preserve the condition wherever that material seeks to serve as a sign of form.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Polish l and paired Indian historical labels
decision.resolution: The checked print has italic l described as having a stroke, not a literal slash. Keep l with a stroke in English; cerebral or lingual names one paired historical class. The note explains articulation cautiously, without importing modern terminology into Humboldt’s text.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Dispositions, habits and the effect of writing
decision.resolution: Use linguistic dispositions and habits, retaining both general capacities and acquired use. The precision gained through written signs acts back upon speaking and becomes the nations’ possession.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Exclude syllables or delete them in an utterance
decision.resolution: Use exclude: the following sentence concerns the inventory of possible syllables. Elision in a particular utterance is not established by ausstossen here.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Originally separate syllables and later contraction
decision.resolution: Keep the contrast between more developed and more original language as the author’s comparison. Do not infer a reconstructed historical sequence from the comparison alone.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Internal structure and meeting consonants
decision.resolution: Retain the scope over word beginnings, endings and internal structure; consonant changes on contact are a particular illustration, not the only rule.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Overlapping names for sound alteration
decision.resolution: Letter change renders Buchstabenverwandlung here; the different German compounds remain recoverable. No fixed distinction between Veränderung and Verwandlung is invented.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Vor dem Verstände: presentation or temporal precedence
decision.resolution: Use as it appears to the understanding, supported by the parallel contrast before the ear/understanding in64. The rejected before understanding intervenes temporal reading remains available in the Codex candidate. This is an interpretation of a compressed construction, not a textual emendation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Indian languages arising from Sanskrit
decision.resolution: Retain the printed historical claim. The next Telinga example is identified as Dravidian Telugu in an attributed translator note; Carey’s cited preface has not been independently checked.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Ideal force and correct articulation
decision.resolution: Use conceptual force and proper articulation of discourse for the understanding, preserving the restriction to parts of one word and the contrast with an apparent auditory whole made from independent words.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: The limited poetic concession
decision.resolution: Preserve the first-person judgment and only insofar as. The advantage is aligning divisions between words and rhythmic divisions, not a general endorsement of cross-word contraction.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Within word boundaries
decision.resolution: Within the bounds of the word means internal restriction, not a change taking place across the word boundary. Preserve the sensory reinforcement of conceptual articulation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Word-whole and distinct sound unity
decision.resolution: Use words as wholes and unity of sound; no independent modern phonological definition of word is supplied. The following qualification about partly shared Sanskrit rules remains in full.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Zeitmass as quantity
decision.resolution: Use quantity throughout this division, with syllabic duration and vowel length explained in the guide. Do not reduce it to vowel length alone or confuse it with accent.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Antecedent of dieselbe
decision.resolution: The feminine pronoun agrees with Sylbe, whereas Zeitmass is neuter. Make the feeling for the syllable explicit; retain the distinction between the sound inventory and its written signs.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Desselben and ihm in the quantity comparison
decision.resolution: Read desselben as quantity and ihm as expression of thoughts, in the contrast with neglect of vowel length. State the referents explicitly and preserve the strong never; the pronoun alternatives remain in candidate notes.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Former refers to rhythm
decision.resolution: Make rhythm, rather than accent, the party potentially harmed by the relationship; quantity’s calm sway is contrasted with forceful discourse and the sharply accentuating understanding.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Whose freedom is preserved
decision.resolution: Retain its freedom provisionally. A local translator note names aesthetic feeling, rhythm and quantity as possible antecedents. The compressed pronoun is not treated as settled by agreement or editorial preference.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Exclusive intention versus later constraints
decision.resolution: Keep exclusively. The note points forward to pronunciation, euphony and the language-specific placement of word accent; do not rewrite the first claim into a weaker modern account.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Tonlos in accentual grouping
decision.resolution: Use unaccented, not silent, voiceless or without lexical tone. The following syllables are drawn into the accented syllable’s domain; the deleted or a word remains solely in the attributed1906 note.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Tongebiete in the local accent account
decision.resolution: Use accentual domains here, because the passage describes grouping around prominence rather than sound inventories or musical pitch regions; the German remains available.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Chinese intonation and organizing accent
decision.resolution: Retain intonation in the historical text and explain the local tone contrast in the guide. The vowel-only assertion remains as printed and receives a sourced, explicitly limited Cantonese qualification.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Discourse accent and isolated language parts
decision.resolution: Use discourse accent consistently for Redeaccent. Its variation with discourse is distinct from the claim that its habitual treatment belongs to the language.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Bis jetzt and surviving accent evidence
decision.resolution: Make the time-bound limit so far explicit. A translator note points to later Vedic descriptions while retaining the separate question of recovering actual delivery from notation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Conceptual unity is not a modern word test
decision.resolution: Keep breathes the unity of the concept and only through accent. Cross-reference the later enclitic grouping rather than assert that audible unity always identifies an independent word.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Exception and the final alsdann
decision.resolution: The exception concerns concepts failing to combine; the causal explanation one element predominates is read as applying when they do combine. Make that scope explicit; the compressed German and Muse’s less explicit alternative remain available.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Word physiognomy and Oxford spelling
decision.resolution: Keep the physiognomy metaphor and its qualification. Use unanalysed, correcting the candidate’s mixed spelling without changing the conceptual claim.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Geltung is standing rather than truth
decision.resolution: Use independent standing, contrasted with attachment, not validity or truth. The account concerns words’ realization and contribution.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Lautgeltung and reduction
decision.resolution: Use sound value for the audible realization altered in enclitic use, not logical force. Preserve the reference to common speakers as Humboldt’s.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Host accent and the second weaker accent
decision.resolution: Retain both possible relocation and acquisition of a second, probably not equally strong, accent, and the dependence of both on particular languages. Orthotonic and enclitic forms remain distinct.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Weighting versus a habitual delivery pattern
decision.resolution: The second delivery method is independent of the first weighting; sense is not wholly sacrificed but is completely subordinated. Preserve both qualifications rather than making the method wholly meaningless.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Verstandesgeltung and contribution
decision.resolution: Use significance for the understanding, not sound volume or truth-validity. Differences concern the degree of prominence given to words and syllables.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Writing recalls rather than preserves sound
decision.resolution: Keep the passing acoustic occurrence distinct from its written reminder and the resulting intellectual analysis. Character as elements renders Elementareigenschaft.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Gliederung and the two benefits
decision.resolution: Keep organization into parts and structure rising from basic parts, preserving both auditory ordering and the understanding’s more vivid analysis. Do not collapse Anschaulichkeit and Vollständigkeit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Scholarly systematization has a stated downside
decision.resolution: Preserve the warning about excessively contrived and systematic treatment and its particular setting: a shift from living popular use to learned use.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Stamping and stages of derivation
decision.resolution: Retain the root-to-word stamping metaphor, followed by inflection and further Taddhita reshaping. Do not turn the loose internal-rule label into a uniform rule across all stages.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: The causal force of weil weniger üblichen
decision.resolution: Preserve fuller because less usual, not less usual because fuller. The printed claim links frequency to fullness; neither a silent omission of weil nor a modern frequency theory is supplied.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D036; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Printed Haugthon spelling
decision.resolution: Retain Haugthon as supplied in the1906 citation and record the spelling issue; no independently checked bibliographic emendation is claimed.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-letters
decision.resolution: “Letters” here are speech-sound elements, not marks on a page; see the terminology guide. Writing is introduced separately in 71. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-clicks
decision.resolution: Modern phonetics classifies clicks as consonants, not as an animal residue added to articulated speech. See the [International Phonetic Association’s chart](https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/IPAcharts/common_files/pdfs/pdfs_IPA_charts_archive/IPA_unitipa_2020.pdf), “Consonants (non-pulmonic)”. This classification does not support Humboldt’s scale of intellectual refinement. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-conceptual-inference
decision.resolution: This moves from the differentiation of sounds to a judgment about concepts. Humboldt offers it as part of his theory; no comparative demonstration is given in this division. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-meaningless
decision.resolution: “Meaningless” here contrasts with an associated concept carried by the sound. It does not mean that an inflection has no grammatical role: the point is to express the relation without adding unrelated lexical content. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-deleted-near
decision.resolution: Deleted after ‘der’: ‘lying close to one another’. (1906 Ed.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-bopp-62
decision.resolution: Bopp’s Lehrgebäude der Sanskrita Sprache, p. 14, no. 20. (Bopp’s Grammar.) (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-cerebral
decision.resolution: “Cerebral” and “lingual” are historical names for consonants made with the tongue tip drawn back, usually called retroflex consonants today. They concern articulation, not a class of mental abilities; see [Whitney, Sanskrit Grammar, §45](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Sanskrit_Grammar_(Whitney)/Chapter_II). (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-understanding
decision.resolution: The phrase “before the understanding” is read here as “as it appears to the understanding”, in line with the parallel contrast between ear and understanding in 64. A temporal reading, “before understanding intervenes”, is also possible, but is less well supported by that parallel. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-thiersch
decision.resolution: Thiersch maintains that the Greeks joined words, as in Sanskrit. (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-carey
decision.resolution: Grammar of the Telinga Language, Preface, p. II. (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-telugu
decision.resolution: “Telinga” is Telugu, a Dravidian language, not a descendant of Sanskrit. The transition from Sanskrit-derived languages to this example therefore needs qualification: compare [Carey’s catalogue record](https://openlibrary.org/books/OL27882132M/A_grammar_of_the_Telinga_language) with [Glottolog’s classification](https://glottolog.org/glottolog?iso=tel). Carey’s cited preface has not been independently checked here. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-haughton
decision.resolution: Haugthon’s Rudiments of Bengali Grammar, p. 147, § 377. (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-bopp-64
decision.resolution: Strictly speaking, the rules for the interior of words are not quite correctly so called. They apply in full only when the root is stamped anew as a word, and in that word’s inflections. Already with the Taddhita suffixes, which further reshape the word thus stamped, the rules for the initial and final letters of different words come into play. Bopp’s Grammar, p. 58, § 85. (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-deleted-signs
decision.resolution: Deleted after ‘dem’ in ‘in dem’ (‘in which’): ‘with or without signs of their own’. (1906 Ed.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-freedom
decision.resolution: The referent of “its freedom” is compressed. It may be aesthetic feeling, rhythm or quantity; the English leaves the reference open rather than assigning it uniquely. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-intention
decision.resolution: The claim of exclusive dependence on intention is Humboldt’s. He immediately adds constraints from pronunciation and euphony, and in 67 treats word accent as belonging to the language; it should not be paraphrased as free choice of the accent on each word. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-deleted-word
decision.resolution: Deleted after ‘syllable’: ‘or a word’. (1906 Ed.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-vowel-tone
decision.resolution: Tone is not confined to vowels in all Chinese varieties. Cantonese has tone-bearing syllabic nasals, such as *m4* “no” and *ng5* “five”, with no vowel; see [Hong Kong Polytechnic University, “Understanding Finals”](https://www.polyu.edu.hk/clc/cantonese/phoneticKnowledge/vowel/recognizingVowel/?lang=en), the syllabic-nasals table. This does not identify the exact varieties covered by Humboldt’s sources. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-chinese
decision.resolution: In Chinese grammars, the intonations are admittedly called modifications of the words, or, what there amounts to the same thing, of the syllables, which is indeed much more appropriate in those grammars. Yet, properly speaking, they rest only on the vowel ending; hence, speaking in the manner of other languages, it is more natural to say that each simple and compound vowel ending can have such and such an intonation, and that the words then take the vowel ending intoned in this or that way according to differences in their meaning. In this way the matter is put on the same footing as the short and long vowels of other languages. (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-sanskrit-accent
decision.resolution: This records the limits of Humboldt’s information, not a present absence of evidence. Later descriptions document accent marks in Vedic texts; see [Whitney, Sanskrit Grammar, §87](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Sanskrit_Grammar_(Whitney)/Chapter_II). Written notation does not by itself recover every detail of spoken delivery. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-word-unity
decision.resolution: The argument links unity of concept with unity of accent. Compare 69, where Humboldt considers several words joining as one accentual group; a group heard as one whole need not simply be one independent word. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-combined-accent
decision.resolution: “When they do combine” makes explicit the reading that conceptual union requires one element to predominate. The final “in that case” in the German could instead be attached to the preceding negative alternative; its reference is not explicit. (Trans.)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader note: sound-source-sanskrit-pronouns
decision.resolution: The Sanskrit pronouns of the first and second persons do have, for certain cases, a second, more frequently used, abbreviated form alongside the full form, whose fullness is due to its less frequent use. But it does not appear that this second form was used exclusively as an enclitic. (Humboldt)

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-letters-alphabet
decision.resolution: A “letter” often means a speech-sound element, and “alphabet” the inventory or system of such sounds. They are not automatically written characters or a modern phoneme inventory. Where writing enters in 62 and 71, written signs are identified separately; Buchstabenschrift is alphabetic writing.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-sound-articulation
decision.resolution: Ton and Laut overlap as “sound”; articulated sound is shaped to carry thought. Geräusch is the accompanying noise Humboldt wants removed, though his evaluation of particular consonants is qualified in the note on 57. Schall in 71 is the transient acoustic occurrence to which the written sign recalls us.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-mental-agency
decision.resolution: These are “mind”, “understanding” and “soul” in this unit. The English keeps the recurring German terms recoverable without turning every lexical difference into a separate modern psychological mechanism. Understanding here names an intellectual capacity, not just successful comprehension of an utterance.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-intellectual-character
decision.resolution: Here the term concerns language’s intellectual character and its relation to thought. The earlier division used “intellectual life” where the bearer was a nation and its orientation; that contextual change does not establish different faculties. “Intellectual cultivation” in 70 renders a different expression, intellectuelle Bildung.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-changes
decision.resolution: The German uses several overlapping expressions for alterations of speech sounds. The contexts include inflection, changes inside words and changes when words meet; these are not automatically historical sound laws or merely spelling changes. The German forms remain available in the linked record.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-linking
decision.resolution: Words can be linked by changes at their boundaries and by contraction. Humboldt distinguishes changes joining parts of one word from those joining otherwise independent words, criticizes the latter for obscuring conceptual divisions, and allows a poetic advantage. This is his argument, not a modern rule for counting words.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-quantity
decision.resolution: Quantity concerns timing, including long and short vowels and syllabic duration; it is distinct from accent. Consonants also enter the argument in 65, so syllabic timing should not be reduced to vowel length alone. Rhythm and accent can support or oppose one another in Humboldt’s account.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-accent
decision.resolution: Accent organizes prominence and groups in speech; word accent belongs to the word, discourse accent varies with delivery. Intonation in the Chinese discussion concerns tone distinctions, not simply sentence melody. These historical categories overlap with modern stress, pitch accent and tone without being identical to them.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-clitics
decision.resolution: Here an enclitic word loses its independent accent and attaches to another word; an orthotonic form has its own accent. Humboldt’s point is that an independent word’s pronunciation and accent can change through attachment, which complicates the picture of one word as one audible whole.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-derivation
decision.resolution: In the note on 64, a root is first “stamped” into a word and the word is then reshaped further by Taddhita suffixes. The metaphor distinguishes stages of formation; the note warns that the rules loosely called “internal” do not apply uniformly at every stage.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-euphony
decision.resolution: Euphony means pleasing sound as assessed in the argument. Roughness, purity and refinement are Humboldt’s aesthetic and developmental evaluations; they are not measurements of a people’s intellectual capacities. Keep the sensory description distinct from the value attached to it.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 policy under D036; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: sound-geltung
decision.resolution: Geltung varies with its bearer: the conceptual force of language, the sway of quantity, a word’s independent standing, or its significance for the understanding. Lautgeltung concerns audible realization. These are related contributions or kinds of standing, not uniformly logical validity.

evidence.locator: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Sanskrit_Grammar_(Whitney)/Chapter_II; §45(lingual/cerebral articulation),§87(Vedic accent marks),§§92–96(word accent and its limits)
evidence.statement: Relevant complete numbered paragraphs read in the primary-work transcription; no complete grammar reread or new print collation. The historical cerebral/lingual terminology describes tongue position; later scholarship documents Vedic accent. More than one accented syllable is discussed in§94, but this alone does not refute Humboldt’s narrower claim about two exactly equal accents.

Complete relevant table and final examples read through web tool. Cantonese has syllabic nasals with tones, so a vowel-only statement is not valid as a general claim about all Chinese varieties. It does not identify exactly which varieties Humboldt’s sources described.

evidence.excerpt: “Letters” here are speech-sound elements, not marks on a page; see the terminology guide. Writing is introduced separately in 71.
evidence.statement: Prevent written characters from replacing speech sounds in the argument.

evidence.excerpt: Modern phonetics classifies clicks as consonants, not as an animal residue added to articulated speech. See the [International Phonetic Association’s chart](https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/IPAcharts/common_files/pdfs/pdfs_IPA_charts_archive/IPA_unitipa_2020.pdf), “Consonants (non-pulmonic)”. This classification does not support Humboldt’s scale of intellectual refinement.
evidence.statement: Qualify the explicit assimilation of legitimate speech sounds to animal noise.

evidence.excerpt: This moves from the differentiation of sounds to a judgment about concepts. Humboldt offers it as part of his theory; no comparative demonstration is given in this division.
evidence.statement: Mark the inference rather than making a measurement of conceptual clarity out of a sound inventory.

evidence.excerpt: “Meaningless” here contrasts with an associated concept carried by the sound. It does not mean that an inflection has no grammatical role: the point is to express the relation without adding unrelated lexical content.
evidence.statement: Prevent absence of substantive content from becoming absence of grammatical function.
